source.title_on_document: Think First, ChatGPT Later: Guiding Human–AI Collaboration for Learning Gains in Independent Human Creativity

supplement.where: No supplementary material is cited. Appendices A to E (task instructions, AUT flexibility categories, sample responses in Tables 7 and 8) are inside this PDF (pp. 33-41). Data and analysis code: https://osf.io/t7an8/overview?view_only=fc490583cdc8458e8b895b29e4df2345 (p. 41, Data Availability).
supplement.holds: Nothing outside the PDF holds statistics; arm means, SDs, Bonferroni p values, and Cohen's d are printed in the main text (pp. 20-22). Participant-level data are on OSF.

paper_design_summary: University students in Singapore (N = 196 analyzed) were randomly assigned in a lab to solve a 12-minute product improvement task (improve a stuffed bunny) alone (human-only), with free use of ChatGPT-4 (general-AI), or with a guided 'think first, ChatGPT later' protocol (regulated-AI: 3 min own ideas, 6 min ChatGPT with sample prompts, 3 min independent refinement). All participants then solved a 12-minute product invention task (a language-learning game) without ChatGPT. Two blind experts rated each solution for originality, usefulness, and elaboration on 1-7 scales.

studies.label: Lab experiment: product improvement task (AI available by arm), then product invention task (no AI)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Learning group for the product improvement task: human-only (no ChatGPT), general-AI (free ChatGPT-4 use), or regulated-AI (guided 'think first, ChatGPT later' use of ChatGPT-4 with sample prompts)
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three learning groups: human-only (control condition; n = 64), general-AI (n = 67), or regulated-AI (n = 65).

arms.name: human-only
arms.description: Solved the product improvement task independently with no other tabs or windows open; then the product invention task alone.

arms.name: general-AI
arms.description: Freely used ChatGPT-4 in a split-screen window for the full 12 minutes of the product improvement task; then the product invention task alone.

arms.name: regulated-AI
arms.description: Phase 1: 3 min generating own ideas alone; Phase 2: 6 min interacting with ChatGPT-4 as a brainstorming and feedback partner, with seven sample prompts shown; Phase 3: 3 min refining and submitting the best idea alone. Then the product invention task alone.

participants.exclusions: 197 students took part; one participant who failed to adhere to the experimental instructions was excluded, leaving 196. The arm counts printed with the random-assignment sentence (64, 67, 65) sum to 196, so they are post-exclusion counts; the paper does not say which arm the excluded participant was in, and does not report a count at assignment.
participants.who: University students aged 18-29 (M = 21.62; 125 female, 67 male, 5 undisclosed among the 197) from diverse majors at a large public university, paid in course credit or money
participants.quote: Outcomes reported below are based on data from 196 participants; one participant who failed to adhere to the experimental instructions was excluded from analyses.

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT-4 (GPT-4 version of ChatGPT via the web interface, ChatGPT Plus subscription, default parameters, memory/model training switched off)
ai_tool.how_used: General-AI: free use of ChatGPT-4 for the whole 12-minute task, told to give clear, detailed prompts. Regulated-AI: own ideas first, then 6 minutes with ChatGPT-4 as a brainstorming and feedback partner guided by seven sample prompts (refine, elaborate, combine, find weaknesses, compare), then independent final write-up. No AI for anyone on the product invention task (pp. 13-14; p. 42 Reproducibility Note; Table 1 p. 10).

task.description: Product improvement task: propose one best creative (original and useful) idea to improve an ordinary 30 cm stuffed bunny for Mattel (Appendix A). Product invention task: invent a new game to help adults and university students learn basic foreign-language vocabulary, with title, materials, and gameplay (Appendix B). Baseline AUT (car tire, 2 min) before assignment.
task.duration: 12 min per creative task; AUT 2 min; whole session about 30 min (pp. 9, 11, 13)

outcomes.name: Originality of the product improvement solution (during intervention)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two trained experts, blind to condition, rated each solution 1-7 for originality following the Consensual Assessment Technique, in a different random order per rater; mean of the two ratings used; consistency ICC = .958 (p. 15-16). Analyzed in a 3 (group) x 2 (task) mixed ANOVA with Bonferroni-corrected simple effects.

eligibility.reason: Individuals were randomly assigned to no AI, free ChatGPT-4 use, or guided ChatGPT-4 use on a creative product improvement task (p. 8); 196 people analyzed, 64 to 67 per arm (p. 8); originality, usefulness, and elaboration of each solution were rated by two blind experts (pp. 15-16). The study supplies with_ai estimates (product improvement task) and after_ai estimates (product invention task done without AI in the same session).

one_line_finding: With ChatGPT available, free use raised expert-rated originality over no AI (4.08 vs 3.06, d = 0.79) while guided use did not (3.30, d = 0.18); on a later task without AI, guided users were more original than both no-AI (3.42 vs 2.63, d = 0.52) and free-use (2.69, d = 0.48) participants, and free users did not differ from no-AI (d = 0.04) (p. 20).
open_questions: The arm counts printed with the random-assignment sentence (64 + 67 + 65 = 196) equal the analyzed total, and 197 people took part; the arm of the one excluded participant and the count at assignment are not stated (p. 8).

Cohen's d is printed for each pairwise contrast, but the paper does not say which standard deviation it uses; for regulated-AI vs general-AI on the improvement task the printed sign is negative while the text says general-AI was higher (p. 20), so the d sign convention appears to be regulated minus general.
The after_ai outcome is measured on a different and, per the authors, more complex task (product invention) in the same roughly 30-minute session, not on a delayed repeat of the same task.
candidates.json lists a 2025 NUS bachelor's thesis by Qiu as another version of this work; the PDF does not mention it, so the shared sample is not confirmed here.
Elaboration is a paper-named primary outcome but is used as a confound check, not as a creativity measure (p. 15); whether it enters the with_ai or after_ai views needs a decision.
notes: Outcomes not listed because they are not scored on the output or answer none of the three questions: baseline AUT fluency and flexibility (pre-assignment balance check, p. 19, Table 3); self-assessed originality and usefulness on both tasks, subjective experience, creative self-efficacy, and metacognition (self-report, exploratory, pp. 27-28, Table 3); ChatGPT prompt counts by type for the two AI arms (Table 5, pp. 23-24), correlations with invention-task creativity (Table 6, p. 25), and a mediation model in which 'improve own initial ideas' prompts mediate the regulated-AI vs general-AI originality gap on the invention task (indirect effect 0.61, 95% CI [0.12, 1.19]; usefulness 0.13, [-0.27, 0.62]; p. 26, Fig. 3). Within-group changes from task 1 to task 2 are also reported (pp. 20, 22) but are not AI contrasts. All creativity analyses are participant-level (one solution per person, mean of two raters) in 3 x 2 mixed ANOVAs with Bonferroni-corrected pairwise tests; Fig. 2 error bars are standard errors (figure only). Per codebook rule 3, the general-AI arm is closest to free chatbot use for the with_ai and after_ai ai_vs_bau primary records.
